text: Good evening, everyone. My name is Lauren Chernov, and I'm calling this Specialized Programs & Centers Committee meeting on Tuesday, September 15, 2026, to order. And we have a full house. You cannot see us, but it is a full house today, so we are so thankful that you are here. I'm joined by my colleague, Mr. Pepper. And our apologies in advance, we have had a very long day. Many of us have been together, talking budget for almost eight hours today.

So we're a little slap happy. So we're going to do our best, though. We're going to have a good time because it looks like there are some fun things happening in the room. So we are very excited to have you. And with that, we will start with public comment. We have one public commenter tonight. It is Mr. Paul Vickers. And you will have three minutes, Mr. Vickers, and start when you're ready. Thank you, Ms. Chernov, and thank you, Mr. Pepper. So I am Paul Vickers, I'm the principal of Hillsboro Charter Academy, and I'm here

to talk about perimeter fencing that you'll find on 60 out of 62 elementary schools here in Loudoun County. The two schools that don't have the perimeter fencing are our school, Hillsboro Charter Academy, and also Middleburg Community Charter School. And so the reason why I wanted to bring this to everyone's attention right now is that a couple of days ago, I received a report that the safety and security team

had partnered with Armored One to conduct a third-party security assessment for all schools. And our lack of a perimeter fencing was actually mentioned no fewer than six times in the report as it's actually listed as both a weakness and a priority, something that needs to happen. In fact, it says, quote, "Particular attention should be given to the roadway and

traffic loop adjacent to the basketball courts and playground, where vehicles have direct access to high-occupancy student activity areas." If you know where Hillsboro Charter Academy is, we are on the first circle, heading west on Route 9 as you come into Hillsboro. So we are actually a school that if you drive 10 minutes down the road, you literally can leave our state and be in either West Virginia or Maryland.

And I think prioritizing student safety is obviously something that our school district does exceptionally well. It doesn't make a lot of sense to me. I've been working in the school system since 1991. All three of my children went to school here. My wife has been teaching and working in the school system for 37 years. And we just don't understand why our students, we have 144 students at our school, 300 on our wait list, and we just don't really understand why our

children aren't seen in the same light as all the other children in the school system. If security and safety fencing, perimeter fencing is important at 60 elementary schools, I would submit to you that it's important at all elementary schools. And that's the reason why I'm here. And I love this school system, and I love what we are doing for children, but I think we're missing the mark on this one. Thank you.

outsourcing and trying to find the materials and the supplies that they need. It's assembling everything together, making sure we have all the supplies we need. I think there's going to be a lot of packing for that. I think there's going to be a lot of looking at needs assessments across the schools that they support. I think there's going to be a lot of inventory. So what happens is they ship those things out to the schools. We have a closed-loop system, so we follow up to say, "Did you receive this? Has it been helpful?" I think we've forecasted some of the other things, packing events that we want to have,

and things like that. I don't know if there's anything else you want to add. So I do think a lot of it is assembly, packing, distribution, going out.
